title: THING//MANIA hybrid AC-01: GROOVE FIRST
description: A+C hybrid, 80% SOCK SLIDE / 20% LOW BATTERY CHOIR. Thesis: an irresistibly funky arcade band is interrupted by mischievous singing appliances. SOCK SLIDE stays the foundation (riff, swing, whistle, clav, kit). Bars 1-2: riff and whistle hook. Bars 3-4: an appliance answers the whistle with C's chant moved into E minor - ba (E) da (G) DEE (A#) - and the DEE rides the bass's Bb->B bend three octaves up; the whistle then borrows that bend. Bars 5-6: a second appliance (the kettle) harmonizes the tag in parallel fourths; then the band stops dead for one beat while the toaster sings the tag at double speed, and the band slams back in on the bend. Bars 7-8: A's F13 slip, handed to a close-harmony choir that holds the chord, then sags one semitone onto E as its battery dies - the sag is the slide home - and a kitchen-timer ding on the downbeat restores power.

tracks.description: A's squelch bass riff (unchanged sound, same choke and processing).
Parallel high-passed, driven copy of the bass so the riff carries on phone speakers (2 dB hotter than A).
A's whistle: hook, pickups and answers. Panned 0.3 and 1 dB up, which keeps A's level under the balance pan law.
The same whistle without its dotted-eighth echo, for the phrases that hand over to an appliance: the echo would land exactly on the appliance's entry.
Em9 stabs on the swung off-beats; they step aside whenever an appliance sings.
A's kick, locked to the bass on 1 and 3-and.
Parallel crunch bus: the kick and snare hits again, high-passed and driven hard so the kit has bite and reads on phones.
Swung 16ths accenting the off-beat eighths; open hat on 4-and in odd bars, choked by the next closed hat.
The lead appliance (toaster): the ba-da-DEE tag in bars 3 and 5, sung at double speed into the bar-6 hole.
A second appliance harmonizing the tag a fourth below in bar 5 (planing, after C).
Close-harmony choir on the bar-8 slip: G4 C5 D5 (with the clav F13) held one beat, then a coherent continuation from the same source position sags one semitone onto F#4 B4 C#5 at the downbeat.
